record.context_brief: First-order asymptotics of Wilf partition counts
record.original_question: Let f(n) denote the number of partitions of the integer n for which every nonzero multiplicity of a part is distinct. Determine the first-order asymptotic behavior of f(n) itself, not just of ln f(n).

evidence.quote: A Herculean task would be to find the first-order asymptotic description of f(n) itself.

artifact.self_contained_problem: For a positive integer $n$, let $f(n)$ denote the number of integer partitions $\lambda$ of $n$ with the following property: writing $\lambda$ in the form $\lambda = (1^{m_1} 2^{m_2} 3^{m_3} \cdots)$, where $m_i \ge 0$ is the multiplicity of the part $i$ in $\lambda$, all the nonzero multiplicities $m_i$ are pairwise distinct. (For example, $5 = 1+2+2$ qualifies because the multiplicities $1$ and $2$ of the parts $1$ and $2$ are distinct, while $4 = 1+1+2+2$ does not, since both $1$ and $2$ have multiplicity $2$.) It is known that $\log f(n) \sim \tfrac{1}{3}(6n)^{1/3}\log n$ as $n \to \infty$. Determine the first-order asymptotic behavior of $f(n)$ itself, i.e., find an explicit function $g(n)$ such that $f(n) \sim g(n)$ as $n \to \infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: Available work by Fill–Janson–Ward and independently Kane–Rhoades establishes the first-order asymptotics of $\log f(n)$, with refinements giving $\log f(n) = \tfrac{1}{3}(6n)^{1/3}\log n - \tfrac{1}{2}(6n)^{1/3}\log\log n + O(n^{1/3})$. No source found that establishes a sharp first-order asymptotic equivalent for $f(n)$ itself; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Partitions with Distinct Multiplicities of Parts: On An "Unsolved Problem" Posed By Herbert Wilf
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes lead-order asymptotics for ln f(n) but notes finding the asymptotics of f(n) itself would be a 'Herculean task.'
status_evidence.claim: Only log f(n) asymptotics known; f(n) asymptotics flagged as much harder.

status_evidence.title: The number of fixed points of Wilf's partition involution
status_evidence.snippet: Provides refined asymptotic for log f(n) and log F(n), still at logarithmic level only.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work refines log f(n) asymptotics but does not give f(n) asymptotically.
